title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: Likely YSO extinction event. Faded progressively after 2015. Located in HII region IRAS 12331-6134 & cluster [DBS2003] 78.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: A long-lasting dip from 2010-2017, recovered only in 2018. 2MASS Ks=12.99, H=15.01. DENIS K=12.45. RR YSO candidate.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: Irregular variation, somewhat ambiguous as dipper or eruptive YSO. Heavily blended with companion when faint. Ks=12.0 in 2MASS, In [DBS2003] 95 cluster and HII region. Mid-infrared excess in Glimpse & MIPSGAL.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: Dipper. Deep fade from 2011-2012, faint in 2013, recovered in 2014 and then brightened further in 2017. RR YSO candidate. Numerous star formation indicators in SIMBAD. WCI shows location in an IRDC.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: Irregular variation, ~2 mag rise in  2014 then a 4 mag fade from 2016-2018, remaining faint in 2019. Not in 2MASS PSC. The brightest dipping giant in the mid-IR. Red WISE cand Spitzer/GLIMPSE-II colours (W1-W2=2.3, W2-W4=5.1).

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: Constant brightness except in 2015, when it was undetected. Likely a giant star eclipsed by a circumsecondary disc, see Smith et al., 2021, MNRAS, 505, 1992 and Appendix I.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: Faded steeply from Ks=13 to ~17 from 2011 to 2013. Rarely detected (K~17) after 2013, in good seeing. UKIDSS K=13.58 in 2006. Not in 2MASS PSC.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: Light curve resembles an eruptive YSO. Unseen in 2010-2013. Seen in 2014 at K=17.1, rose to K=13 by 2017 and remained bright afterward. Not in 2MASS PSC. Spectroscopically confirmed giant in GLK

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: Slow 9 yr fade from Ks=11.6 in 2010 to Ks~16 in 2019. UKIDSS K=11.05 in 2006. 2MASS Ks=10.63.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: A dipper with a 1200 day dip by 4 mag, minimum in 2013-2014. Then a second dip with minimum jn 2016. Flat spectrum YSO in SPICY. Also a RR YSO candidate. Projected near the Galactic centre.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: Little variability from 2010-2015 (Ks~11.5). Faded to Ks~15.6 by 2019. UKIDSS K=11.54 in 2006. Not in 2MASS PSC. Listed as variable in Matsunaga et al.( 2009) but no period could be fitted, see main text.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: K~10.5 from 2010-2013, then faded slowly to Ks~14 in 2018-2019. UKIDSS K=10.94 in 2006. 2MASS Ks=10.74.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: A dipper with short and long timescale variation. Deep dip in 2013, brighter before and after. Dip finished by 2017, then stable at Ks=12. 2MASS Ks=11.87. Projected on BGPSv2 G000.164+00.071 mm core, likely a coincidence, given the CMZ location.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: Faded from Ks=13.0 to 15.5 from 2010-2012. Unseen in 2013-2014 (blended). Recovered after 2014 to Ks~13. UKIDSS K=12.54 in 2006. 2MASS Ks=12.71.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: Resembles a FUor outburst, save for a 1.5 mag dip before the rise. Brightest VVV datum is Ks=12.3 in 2019. UKIDSS K=12.22 in 2006. 2MASS Ks=11.73. Spectroscopically confirmed giant in GLK. WCI shows location in an Infrared Dark Cloud.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: Faded from Ks=14.2 from 2010-2014, rose steeply from 2014-2015, then slowly to Ks=12.8 in 2018. UKIDSS K=16.02 in 2006. Not in 2MASS PSC. Spectroscopically confirmed giant in GLK

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: Almost constant, Ks=11.9, from 2010-2016 then faded monotonically to Ks~16.6 by 2019. UKIDSS K=11.91 in 2006. Not in 2MASS PSC. Listed as variable in Matsunaga et al. (2009) but no period could be fitted, see main text.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: Ks=11.8 in 2010. faded slowly, then showed a deep dip from 2012-2014 (dropping out) before recovering, UKIDSS K=11.74 in 2006. 2MASS Ks=11.08. Spectroscopically confirmed giant in GLK.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: Slow fade from 2010-2014, then a dip dip. Started to recover in 2018. Some short timescale variability. UKIDSS K=12.14 in 2007. 2MASS Ks=11.83. Projected on submm source AGAL G001.203+00.167, likely a coincidence, given the CMZ location.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: Dipping behaviour seen on timescales from months to years. Brightest VVV datum Ks=13 in 2016. UKIDSS K=15.66 in 2006. 2MASS Ks=10.87. Spectroscopically confirmed giant in GLK. Not detected by WISE but WCI shows the location is at the edge of a very small 12um bubble.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: A slow fade from 2010 (Ks=13.1) to 2014 then a deep dip to Ks>17 by 2018, often dropping out. UKIDSS K=12.37 in 2007. 2MASS Ks=12.12.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: Ks~12 in 2010, dipped to K~16 in 2011, recovering in 2013. Ks~12 from 2014, with only low amplitude changes. 2MASS Ks=12.37.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: Faded steeply from Ks=12 in 2011 to Ks=17 in 2013, then often dropping out until recovering from 2017. UKIDSS K=12.06 in 2006. 2MASS Ks=11.84.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: Almost constant, Ks~13 to 13.4, except for a ~4 mag dip in 2015. Dip is asymmetric. UKIDSS K=13.56 in 2007. Not in 2MASS PSC.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: Irregular light curve with long and short term dipping behaviour. Brightest VVV datum Ks~10.2 in 2019. UKIDSS K=10.33 in 2007. 2MASS Ks=9.52. Spectroscopically confirmed giant in GLK.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: Slow, ~5 mag rising trend from 2010 to 2015, only slight changes thereafter, at Ks~11.8. Faint, uncatalogued UKIDSS detection in 2007. 2MASS Ks=13.25. Spectroscopically confirmed giant in GLK. Projected on BGPS G003.074+00.344 mm core and ATLASGAL source.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: A deep dip in 2012, otherwise constant. Better sampled by OGLE in I band. A giant star eclipsed by a circumsecondary disc, see Smith et al., 2021, MNRAS, 505, 1992 and Appendix I.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: Non-variable (Ks=12.8) before 2015. Deep dip from 2015-2018, recovered in 2019. UKIDSS K=12.73 in 2006. 2MASS Ks=12.65.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: A dipper, 3.5 mag fainter than usual in 2016 but ~1mag irregular intra-year variation at all other times. In AGAL G007.976-00.357 dense core. Mid-IR excess in Glimpse II. Simbad shows many SF indicators.

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: KH 15D-like periodically dipping binary YSO with 2 peaks per 59 d period. See main text and appendix E. In NGC 6530, Lagoon Nebula cluster. Listed incorrectly as a dwarf nova in Mroz et al. (2015)

title: The Most Variable VVV Sources: Eruptive Protostars, Dipping Giants in the Nuclear Disc and Others
notes: Shows several ~1 yr highly structured dips of 1 to 2 yr duration. 2MASS Ks=12.47. DENIS K=12.26. Published as an emission line star near HII region IC 1396 (Ogura et al., 2002, AJ, 123, 2597). Gaia EDR3 distance ~1 kpc (5 sigma parallax).
